topic:
We are evaluating the business plan and operational structure for launching BoardRunner.ai as a standalone SaaS product. BoardRunner is an AI advisory board platform — structured multi-agent deliberation, not chatbot. It is 90% built inside Mission Control and needs to be extracted, packaged, priced, and shipped. We have two planning docs: a 7-day launch plan and a Paperclip company plan with an 8-agent team. The board needs to stress-test pricing, go-to-market strategy, target customer, team structure, and technical approach. Key context: we already have the domain (boardrunner.ai), the product works, and we want to reach $10K MRR within 90 days.

Key questions for the board:
1. Is $29/$79/$199 the right pricing? Should there be a free tier?
2. Extract from Mission Control vs fresh build — which and why?
3. Who are the first 10 paying customers? How do we actually reach them?
4. Is Product Hunt the right launch channel, or direct outreach first?
5. 3 QA agents out of 8 total on the Paperclip team — right allocation?
6. Can we realistically hit $10K MRR in 90 days? What has to be true?
7. What is the single biggest risk that kills this?

Reference: Pricing plan is Free ($0, 2 sessions/mo), Starter ($29, 15 sessions), Pro ($79, 50 sessions), Team ($199, 150 sessions/5 seats). Tech plan is to extract from existing Mission Control Next.js app into standalone Vercel deployment with separate Supabase project. GTM plan includes Product Hunt, Hacker News, IndieHackers, and direct founder outreach. Target customers: fund managers, startup founders, agency owners with recurring decision cadences. The product already has roundtable, competitive ideation, review loop modes, dynamic AI personas, personality traits, moderator, session memory, action items, export, and 6 templates shipped.
